assumptions: Footnote 5 elaborates paragraph 14's assurance content while preserving its express request condition for demonstration.
The formalization tests only the activation condition for paragraph 14 demonstration, not performance, confirmation, licence status or overall compliance.

citations.quote: Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

5 Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

Product Providers should, upon SFC’s request, obtain third party audit or verification on the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and integrity of the smart contracts.
Product Providers should, upon SFC’s request, obtain satisfactory legal opinion to support its application.

node.f189039671da0fc054c157bd.distinction: This reading gives operative effect to the request phrase in paragraph 14 despite its omission from footnote 5. No request leaves confirmation and underlying duties in place but does not activate demonstration under the selected control.

questions: Does the SFC-satisfaction standard attach only to demonstration, as its placement suggests?
Does high confidence attach only to the smart-contract proposition, as its placement suggests, or also to compliance with paragraphs 10–13?
node.f189039671da0fc054c157bd.statement: [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] Within the Product Provider scope, true means paragraph 14's request condition for demonstration is satisfied; false means that condition is not satisfied. Confirmation remains unconditioned by a request. Both actions concern management and operational soundness, ownership record keeping and smart-contract integrity; footnote 5 sets a minimum content of compliance with paragraphs 10–13 and absence of contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with high confidence. The strongest grammatical reading attaches SFC satisfaction to demonstration and high confidence to the smart-contract proposition, although broader attachment remains unresolved. With no request, demonstration is not activated on this reading; substantive duties and confirmation remain. Paragraph 15 separately conditions obtaining third-party audit or verification on a request and covers the same three subjects. Paragraph 16 separately conditions obtaining a satisfactory legal opinion supporting the application on a request. Neither provision establishes a routine audit or opinion requirement in the absence of its request.

node.f189039671da0fc054c157bd.unit_of_assessment: Paragraph 14 demonstration activation for one Product Provider's tokenisation arrangement.
node.f189039671da0fc054c157bd.temporal_basis: Whether the applicable request has been made by assessment; no performance deadline is determined.
node.f189039671da0fc054c157bd.true_means: The demonstration trigger is satisfied, not the demonstration requirement itself. Demonstration concerns soundness, ownership records and smart-contract integrity with footnote 5's minimum content. SFC satisfaction most naturally attaches to demonstration and high confidence to the smart-contract proposition, with broader attachment unresolved. A request solely for audit, verification or legal opinion does not automatically count; those duties have separate request conditions.
node.f189039671da0fc054c157bd.false_means: No applicable request activates paragraph 14 demonstration. Confirmation and substantive duties remain; absence of a request does not establish compliance or satisfactory performance.
